subject.title: perf(models-config): unify auth-profile fingerprint cache + targetProvider short-circuit

question: After the synchronous contention defect is fixed, should models-config adopt this content/SQLite fingerprint plus provider-scoped structural short-circuit as its canonical routing trust boundary?
rationale: The shortcut decides when auth/provider discovery may be skipped and changes how unreadable persisted auth state affects routing; implementation correctness alone cannot choose whether that added complexity is the intended permanent policy.

options.title: Adopt after repair
options.body: Fix the blocking read, refresh onto main, and retain the scoped fail-closed validation with exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep warm cache only
options.body: Adopt canonical auth fingerprinting but defer the cold provider/model short-circuit to reduce the routing trust surface.

options.title: Retain current main
options.body: Decline the optimization if the added cache and validation complexity is not worth the measured performance gain.

recommendation.title: Adopt after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the blocking read, refresh onto main, and retain the scoped fail-closed validation with exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant current-main SQLite migration and explicit event-loop-stall hardening both trace to this owner, making them the strongest available decision router.
